For Fall 2026 full-semester classes, classes begin on August 26, 2026. The last day to add or drop a full-semester class with 100% tuition refund is September 1, 2026. The calendar lists the start date as “Full and Session I Courses - Classes Begin” and the add/drop deadline as “Full Semester Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund.” Academic Calendar

Academic Calendar

For Saturday, September 26, 2026, the published Saturday Roadrunner Express shows these Garden State Plaza options: from campus, the afternoon trip that serves Garden State Plaza leaves at 1:40 PM and reaches Garden State Plaza at 2:15 PM. For an evening return from Garden State Plaza, the published stop times are 6:00 PM (returning to campus at 6:35 PM), 8:00 PM (returning to campus at 8:45 PM), and 10:30 PM (returning to campus at 11:00 PM). Transportation Services

If you want a shorter visit, there is also a later outbound trip that serves Garden State Plaza: it leaves campus at 5:25 PM and reaches Garden State Plaza at 6:00 PM, then returns to campus at 6:35 PM on that same run. The published 3:00 PM, 4:40 PM, 6:50 PM, and 8:55 PM campus departures do not list Garden State Plaza among their stops. Transportation Services

For your plan, the simplest afternoon-to-evening combination is usually 1:40 PM from campus to Garden State Plaza, then either the 8:00 PM or 10:30 PM Garden State Plaza stop back, depending on how long you want to stay.

This is the published timetable only; live delays and holiday-related changes are not confirmed here. Transportation Services

Yes. Ramapo lists an Environmental Science BS major in the School of Science, Nursing, and Health. It also lists an Environmental Science Minor, and there is a separate Environmental Studies Minor in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. Ramapo Programs Ramapo Programs Ramapo Programs

For meeting students with similar interests, two student organizations that fit well are 1Step and RCNJ Birding. 1Step describes itself as Students Together for Environmental Progress and focuses on sustainability, environmental issues, recycling, waste awareness, and support for the Ramapo Green initiative. RCNJ Birding says it is for students interested in birds, ecology, and habitat conservation, and aims to build community around those interests.
